items.description: A workspace for running several coding agents at once, each in its own Git worktree, with your own model subscriptions and a mobile app for supervising runs remotely.

items.name: mj12bot.com
items.description: The documentation site for MJ12bot, the web crawler operated by Majestic. It exists to explain the crawler to webmasters deciding whether to allow it.

items.name: mdaemon.com
items.description: MDaemon Technologies, a long-established vendor of self-hosted email server and security software aimed at organisations that will not use a hosted mailbox provider.

items.description: The Chinese site of OpenResty Inc., which builds on the widely deployed OpenResty web platform and sells two enterprise products: Edge for distributed traffic management and XRay for dynamic tracing of production systems.

items.description: The documentation site for MJ12bot, the web crawler operated by Majestic. It exists to explain the crawler to webmasters deciding whether to allow it.

items.name: crmne/fastpotify
items.description: A Spotify desktop client written in Rust for Linux, macOS and Windows, covering the full library, local playback and Spotify Connect. The claim is that it is markedly lighter than the official Electron app.

items.name: sapientinc/PRAXIST
items.description: A framework for research that a computer can run and score without a person in the loop: experiments are expressed so they execute end to end and produce a measurable result.

items.name: IndexFlowing/IndexFlow-core
items.description: Open-source infrastructure for getting pages indexed by search engines at scale. It schedules submissions fairly across many sites at once, runs SEO quality checks inline before a page is submitted, and trips a circuit breaker when an engine's quota runs down.

items.name: seoes/proval
items.description: A code review agent that runs a large language model against pull requests on your own hardware, shipped as a single Docker image. The pitch is reviewing private code without sending it to a third-party service.

items.name: OrRon/EpicInfographics
items.description: A packaged skill that teaches a coding agent to produce infographics, so a chart or diagram can be asked for in conversation rather than designed by hand.

items.name: plannotator/herdr-annotate
items.description: A review tool for agent work: mark up terminal output, documents and an agent's replies, and send the annotations back to the agent as feedback.

items.name: ruoyuw22-byte/NeuroMorph-Assessment
items.description: A pipeline for structural brain MRI that runs CAT12 processing, quantifies brain tissue volumes, renders the visualisations and writes the report automatically.

items.name: SenteLabsAI/OpenExecutive
items.description: OpenExecutive is an AI-powered virtual executive team: a single coherent executive persona backed by eight specialist Claude agents, built on FastAPI with a Next.js front end. The idea is that a founder or small team can put a question to one "executive" and have it answered with the specialist reasoning of a full leadership bench behind it.

items.name: tt-a1i/simplify-codebase
items.description: A tool that identifies incidental complexity in a codebase and removes it, with the emphasis on proving behaviour is unchanged rather than trusting the edit.

items.name: kelviq/tare
items.description: A forensics tool for Claude Code usage. It reads the session logs already on the machine to work out where tokens went and why a limit was hit, and does the analysis locally rather than uploading anything.

items.name: gtlhuyidan-sketch/life-ipo
items.description: A Chinese-language personal data system that pulls finance, health, study notes and contacts into one store and runs decisions over the combined record. Framed as taking your own life public, hence the name.

items.name: agentconnect-md/agentconnect
items.description: An open-source, self-hosted alternative to Claude Tag: mention any coding agent from wherever the team already works, and it joins the thread and carries context forward.

items.name: tailscale/tailcat
items.description: Tailscale's own take on netcat: pipe data between two machines over Tailscale's encrypted data plane without routing it through Tailscale's coordination servers.

items.name: MrRockySL/Muro
items.description: Live animated wallpapers for macOS, written natively to keep CPU and memory use low, with a self-updating library and no paid tier.

items.name: robbyant-research/Zero-WAM
items.description: Research code for learning world and action models by watching human video, aimed at letting a robot generalise to tasks it was never explicitly trained on.

items.name: Merit-Systems/OpenInstinct
items.description: An assistant that lives in iMessage rather than in its own app, with a password vault attached so it can act on accounts as well as answer.

items.name: AgriciDaniel/youtubepro
items.description: A local-first research tool for YouTube creators that pulls channel and video data onto your own machine, then drafts scripts and thumbnails against it rather than against a generic prompt.

items.name: buaacyw/code-world-model
items.description: The reference implementation for Code World Model, a model trained to predict what code does when it runs rather than only what it looks like.

items.name: Tencent/WeMM-Embedding
items.description: A family of multimodal embedding models from Tencent's WeChat Vision team, mapping images and text into one vector space for retrieval and cross-modal search.

items.name: patriceckhart/hrdx
items.description: A terminal multiplexer — splitting one terminal window into several sessions — rebuilt around running coding agents rather than shells, and deliberately kept small.

items.name: amagine-ai/Amagine3D
items.description: Generates editable 3D CAD geometry from a written description of what the part has to do, rather than from a sketch or a photograph. The output is meant to be opened and altered, not just rendered.

items.name: only-cli/oc
items.description: Turns any website into a small command-line interface shaped for agents, so a page costs hundreds of tokens to read instead of tens of thousands. A compression step between the web and the context window.

items.name: MengTo/threeui
items.description: A catalogue of open-source interface components built on Three.js, each rendered live on the page with its full source shown beside it.

items.name: LB623/no-negative-echo
items.description: A Codex add-on that writes titles, comments, commit messages and pull request text from the final state of the work rather than from the whole session, so approaches that were tried and rejected stop leaking into what ships.

items.name: paulsp94/omacosy
items.description: Omacosy is a pre-1.0 desktop environment for macOS in the style of Omarchy: tiling windows with a real Super key, a dwindle layout, a purpose-written themed status bar, focus-follows-mouse, trackpad workspace swipes and a live workspace overview. Six self-built Swift binaries in one repository, built and tested on Apple Silicon.

items.name: proliferate-ai/proliferate
items.description: An open-source desktop IDE built around coding agents rather than around a text editor. It runs Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode side by side, lets several agents work in parallel either locally or on a remote machine, and saves the prompt-and-tool sequences that worked as reusable workflows.

items.name: agentrhq/webcmd
items.description: Browser infrastructure for AI agents that watches how a site is navigated and caches what it learns, so repeated visits send a fraction of the page back to the model. The pitch is a cut in token spend rather than new capability.

items.name: mothparkzo6249/TG-Polymarket-bot
items.description: A Telegram bot that watches Polymarket for unusually large trades and pushes them as alerts, with a one-tap option to place the same bet. Copy-trading for prediction markets, with a free public alerts channel alongside the paid path.

items.name: Pinvou/pinvou-agent
items.description: An open-source desktop agent that works against local files and tools rather than in a chat window, aimed at producing finished documents and artefacts instead of replies.

items.name: Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS
items.description: An open-source text-to-speech model built to run at small parameter counts, claiming quality close to much larger systems. Paired with the Audio8 preview weights published on Hugging Face.

items.name: QwenAudio/qwen-audio-agent
items.description: A runtime for voice agents that holds an open audio session while tools run in the background, so the agent keeps speaking instead of going silent during a long call. Latency plumbing rather than a model.

items.name: Optim-Agent/optim-plans
items.description: A planning layer for Claude Code and Codex that makes an agent write a Markdown plan and get it approved before it may execute. It records the decisions taken and enforces explicit gates between steps.

items.name: therepanic/openleetcode
items.description: An open-source reimplementation of LeetCode's test harness, publishing the hidden test cases that the original keeps private so solutions can be checked locally.

items.name: Paritok-official/paritok-4b-v1
items.description: A proxy that sits between a coding agent and the model and compresses the conversation without dropping information the agent still needs. Claims a quarter off the token bill on the first turn, rising past 85% in long sessions, and roughly three times as many turns in the same context window.

items.name: drumih/turbo-fieldfare
items.description: Runs Google's Gemma 4 26B model on any Apple Silicon Mac in about 2 GB of memory, including the 8 GB machines, instead of loading all 14.3 GB. It keeps the shared core and the cache resident and streams only the experts each token actually needs off the SSD. The runtime, installer, command line tool and Mac app are all written in Swift and Metal, built for this one model rather than wrapping MLX or llama.cpp.

items.name: opslane/opslane
items.description: Error tracking that reads real user session recordings, works out which bugs are actually reaching users, and opens a pull request with a proposed fix rather than filing a ticket.

items.name: IndexFlowing/IndexFlow-core
items.description: Open-source infrastructure for getting pages indexed by search engines at scale. It schedules submissions fairly across many sites at once, runs SEO quality checks inline before a page is submitted, and trips a circuit breaker when an engine's quota runs down.

items.name: experientiallabs/experiential
items.description: An open-source gateway that puts one API and one control plane in front of hosted models, open-weight models, local models and your own fine-tunes, so switching provider is a config change rather than a rewrite.

items.name: voronoigo.com
items.description: Go played on a Voronoi diagram instead of a square grid. Same capture and territory rules, but the board is irregular polygons, so shape intuition learned on a 19x19 board stops transferring.

items.name: polign.com
items.description: Memory infrastructure for AI agents that stores the memory in your own object storage rather than the vendor's, and makes it durable, consistent and searchable across sessions.

items.name: rackout.net
items.description: A shared workspace for planning data centre build-outs: rack layouts, cable routes, what depends on what, and the handover to whoever installs it.

items.name: apvcode/Termux-Dev
items.description: A terminal coding agent built to run on Android under Termux as well as on desktop, with separate plan and execute modes, image input and live web search.

items.name: magicpatterns.com
items.description: Generates production-ready interface code from a written prompt, working against your existing design system rather than a generic component library, so what comes out matches what you already ship.

items.name: issacnitin/RealDiff
items.description: Shows what a pull request changes at runtime rather than in the source: it runs both versions and diffs the observed behaviour, so a refactor that quietly alters output cannot pass as cosmetic.

items.name: flostep.dev
items.description: Turns any process into an ordered walkthrough you can share as a link: sketch the steps, present them in sequence, no account needed to try it.

items.name: patriceckhart/hrdx
items.description: A terminal multiplexer — splitting one terminal window into several sessions — rebuilt around running coding agents rather than shells, and deliberately kept small.

items.name: pantsforbirds.com
items.description: The personal site of an engineer writing up problems they have found interesting, mostly long technical posts rather than a product.

items.name: picomq.com
items.description: A message queue that keeps durable real-time streams in S3-compatible object storage and speaks plain HTTP, so there is no broker to run and storage costs what object storage costs.

items.name: ovenpasta/adi2
items.description: A GUI toolkit for Ada that borrows the web's model: interfaces described in XML, styled with CSS, rendered through SDL3.

items.name: dragthelake/ambient-context
items.description: A macOS menu bar app that watches what you are doing and keeps a written log of it, so the record of the day writes itself.

items.name: soverybright.com
items.description: A free tool that takes a logo and produces an HDR JPEG in which chosen colours glow up to seven and a half times brighter than white on HDR displays, and look normal everywhere else.

items.name: jeffhajewski/latticedb
items.description: An embedded knowledge graph database in a single file, combining graph queries, vector search and full-text search for retrieval-augmented applications. SQLite's shape, applied to RAG.

items.name: codecanary.org
items.description: A monitor that watches a website and tells you when it changes or breaks, named for the canary in the coal mine.

items.name: terminal-code.com
items.description: Runs VS Code inside a terminal session, so the editor is usable over SSH or in a tmux pane without a desktop or a browser.

items.description: The largest of the Ornith 1.5 releases at 397 billion parameters, a mixture-of-experts multimodal model built on the Qwen3.5 architecture that takes images and text and returns text.

items.description: Preview weights for Audio8's text-to-speech model at 100 million parameters, with voice cloning. Small enough to be the one people try on a laptop, which is usually why the small variant moves first.

items.description: SenseNova U1.5 at 8 billion parameters, a natively multimodal model that both reads and generates images as well as text, including image editing.

items.description: A draft model for speculative decoding against Qwen3.8 27B, published as GGUF for llama.cpp. It exists to make a larger model faster, not to be used on its own.

items.name: microsoft/Mage-VL
items.description: Microsoft's Mage-VL, a vision-language model that takes images or video alongside text and returns text. Published for image-text-to-text work and video understanding rather than for generating images.

items.name: Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b
items.description: Preview weights for Audio8's text-to-speech model at 600 million parameters, with voice cloning. The larger of the two previews published together.

items.name: unsloth/Kimi-K3-GGUF
items.description: A GGUF conversion of Kimi-K3 quantised by Unsloth for local inference with llama.cpp. Not a new model but a repackaging of an existing one into the format desktop runners expect, which is usually what a download spike on this kind of repository means.

items.name: EschaLabs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Escha-W2
items.description: A 2-bit MLX build of a 35 billion parameter Qwen3.6 mixture-of-experts model, quantised far enough down to fit on Apple silicon.

opslane.com
items.brief: Stars 16 to 35 and HackerNews points 18 to 35 in a day, with comments 4 to 11 — comments growing faster than points, and open issues 7 to 9 behind them. Small numbers, and worth saying so: thirty-five stars is a handful of people. What makes it worth a second look is that all four moved together on a project whose pitch is that it opens the pull request itself, which is a claim people either try or ignore.

items.name: magicpatterns.com
items.brief: HackerNews points 51 to 55 and comments 23 to 25 while traffic rank improved 1.4% the same day. A modest move on all three, but the third one is the interesting one: attention on a link aggregator is cheap and people arriving at the site afterwards is not, and here the two moved together rather than one without the other.
items.description: Generates production-ready interface code from a written prompt, working against your existing design system rather than a generic component library, so what comes out matches what you already ship.

still_moving.name: onepay.com
still_moving.brief: Go-to-market roles 4 to 5 on a board of 39, taking the GTM share of hiring from 10.5% to 12.8%, while traffic rank improved 4.4% the same day. A company that has been hiring engineers beginning to hire sellers is the transition this whole method watches for. One role is thin evidence and the direction is what matters — but nobody posts a role they do not intend to pay for.
still_moving.description: OnePay is a US consumer mobile banking app offering saving, spending, borrowing, credit building and rewards in one account. It is backed by Walmart and aimed at customers underserved by traditional banks, competing with Cash App and Chime rather than with high-street lenders.

still_moving.name: SenteLabsAI/OpenExecutive
still_moving.brief: Stars 642 to 1,650 and forks 40 to 116 in a day, with HackerNews comments 283 to 656. Forks growing faster than stars means people are standing it up rather than bookmarking it, and open issues fell 12 to 5 across the same window — a maintainer keeping pace with the crowd rather than being buried by it.
still_moving.description: OpenExecutive is an AI-powered virtual executive team: a single coherent executive persona backed by eight specialist Claude agents, built on FastAPI with a Next.js front end. The idea is that a founder or small team can put a question to one "executive" and have it answered with the specialist reasoning of a full leadership bench behind it.

still_moving.name: apify/apify-mcp-server
still_moving.brief: Weekly downloads 50,462 to 59,864 and stars 4,733 to 5,085 in a day, with watchers 20 to 23 and forks still climbing. Downloads growing faster than stars is the useful direction here: people are installing it into something rather than marking it to read later, and the prior week's figure rose 22% underneath, so this is a trend rather than one good day.
still_moving.description: The Apify MCP server lets an AI agent reach the thousands of ready-made scrapers, crawlers and automation tools published on the Apify Store, so an assistant can pull data from social media, search engines, maps, e-commerce listings or any other site through one Model Context Protocol connection rather than a bespoke integration per source. Written in TypeScript and maintained by Apify itself.

still_moving.name: swimmingbrain/texbrain
still_moving.brief: HackerNews points 77 to 117 and comments 16 to 27, with stars 117 to 158 and forks 9 to 13 — forks up 44% against stars up 35%. The open issue count went 1 to 0 the same day. Attention and adoption moving together at that ratio, on a repository small enough that four new forks is a third of all of them, is people trying it rather than reading about it.
still_moving.description: Texbrain is a browser-based LaTeX editor with live preview, on-demand package loading and git integration, released as free and open source. It runs entirely client-side: no accounts, no installation and no server to send a document to, which makes it usable for work that cannot leave the machine it was written on. Built in Svelte.

still_moving.name: t8y2/dbx
still_moving.brief: Week-on-week download growth 1.9% to 19.3%, with Homebrew installs 359 to 374 over thirty days. Two unrelated ways of getting the same tool moved together — npm and a package manager people use deliberately — which is harder to arrange than either one alone.
still_moving.description: A desktop database client that speaks to more than 70 systems, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, DuckDB and SQL Server among them, in a 20 MB download. The same build ships as a desktop app, a Docker image and a command line tool, with an AI assistant and an MCP server included. Most clients of this scope are hundreds of megabytes, so the size is the claim being made.

still_moving.name: xpay.sh
still_moving.brief: Its WordPress plugin's download count moved 1,460 to 1,482 while traffic rank improved 1.5% the same day. Small numbers, but the two came from different places: one counts installs on the plugin directory, the other counts people arriving at the site, and neither knows about the other.
still_moving.description: xpay is a service for making an online store legible to AI shopping agents: it audits and adapts a merchant's catalogue, content and checkout so an assistant can read, recommend and buy from it, then reports the orders that came back through that channel. It offers a free agent-readiness audit without signup, and ships a WordPress plugin for WooCommerce stores.

still_moving.name: tobi/walgit
still_moving.brief: Stars 1,192 to 1,662 and forks 63 to 92 in a day, with HackerNews comments going 8 to 58 on a front-page post. Forks climbing faster than stars means people are standing it up rather than bookmarking it, and a three-day-old repository holding a front page while its comment count grows sevenfold is argument, not applause.
still_moving.description: walgit is a git server that runs as a single binary in front of an object store: no database, no leader, no local state that matters. Point it at an S3 or GCS bucket and it serves smart HTTP fetch and push, bundle-uri clones as static files, Git LFS, a browsing web UI and a JSON API, with every machine running it treated as a disposable cache and the bucket as the repository.

still_moving.name: iverify.io
still_moving.brief: Open roles 4 to 5, and engineering roles 1 to 2 — a small board, but it doubled the half of it that builds. Traffic rank improved 1.1% the same day. Hiring is the signal a company pays for months before anything public moves, and a two-person engineering team becoming a four-person one is a decision already taken.
still_moving.description: iVerify is a mobile endpoint detection and response platform for iOS and Android fleets, built by the team that came out of Trail of Bits. It looks for spyware, smishing, SIM swaps and zero-click exploits on employee phones, and it does so without requiring an MDM enrolment, which is what distinguishes it from most mobile device management tooling.

still_moving.name: paulsp94/omacosy
still_moving.brief: Stars 146 to 151 and forks 3 to 4 in a day, with 57 HackerNews points behind 45 comments. Comments running close to points is argument rather than applause, and forks climbing faster than stars is people running it rather than bookmarking it — the open issue count went 1 to 0 the same day.
still_moving.description: Omacosy is a pre-1.0 desktop environment for macOS in the style of Omarchy: tiling windows with a real Super key, a dwindle layout, a purpose-written themed status bar, focus-follows-mouse, trackpad workspace swipes and a live workspace overview. Six self-built Swift binaries in one repository, built and tested on Apple Silicon.
